name: Define what each role may reach, and enforce it on every request rather than by hiding menu items
priorityReason: Every screen, list, report and export in the system is governed by it. Nothing else decides who may reach what.

goal.capability: to define what each role may reach and have it enforced on every request
goal.outcome: a user reaches only what their role permits, whether they use the menu or type the address

postConditions: Each role holds a defined set of permissions, chosen module by module.
Every request was checked against the permission it requires, on the server.
A request without permission was refused whether it came from the menu or from a typed address.
Nothing was protected by hiding a menu item alone.
Users were assigned to roles by the Super Admin, or by the School Admin of a branch where that permission was delegated.

permissions.notes: Creates roles, sets the permissions each holds, and decides which of those permissions is released to a branch (BR-1, BR-3).

permissions.rowScope: Is governed by it and sees none of its configuration.

businessRules.rule: The Super Admin creates a role and selects the permissions it holds, module by module. Permissions themselves are defined by the system and are not created by anybody.

Users are assigned to a role. Assigning a user to a role is itself a permission held by the Super Admin, and is ordinarily delegated to the School Admin of each branch, who is the person present when somebody joins.

Where it is delegated, a School Admin assigns users only within their own branch, only to roles at or below their own, and cannot grant themselves or anybody else a permission the Super Admin has not released to that branch.
On every request the system checks the user's role against the permission required. The check runs on the server, on every request, without exception.
Requests without permission are refused, whether reached from the menu or by direct address. Hiding a menu item is not access control; it is decoration over an address anybody can type.
A refusal returns the same message whatever the reason, so a refusal does not confirm that the record exists.
The role a user holds is held on their branch assignment, not on the user, so one person may hold different roles at different branches.
A role is never deleted while a user holds it. It is deactivated once nobody does, and stays readable since the audit trail references it.
The Super Admin cannot revoke their own ability to administer roles, since nobody could then restore it.

transitions.condition: No user holds it any longer. It stays readable (BR-8).

basicFlow.navigation: Login → Settings → Roles → Create a role
basicFlow.userAction: Creates the role and selects the permissions it holds, module by module.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Records the role and its permission set.

basicFlow.navigation: Role permissions → Release to a branch
basicFlow.userAction: Decides which of those permissions is released to a branch, so a School Admin there may grant it.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Limits what a School Admin can grant to what has been released to their branch.

basicFlow.navigation: Settings → Branch users → Assign a role
basicFlow.userAction: Assigns a user to a role.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Restricts a School Admin to their own branch, to roles at or below their own, and to permissions released to that branch.
Checks the user's role against the permission the request requires, on the server, on every request.
Refuses a request without permission whether it came from the menu or from a typed address, returning the same message whatever the reason.

basicFlow.userAction: Deactivates a role no user holds any longer.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Refuses while any user holds it, and keeps the role readable.

alternateFlows.condition: The School Admin assigns a user at their own branch
alternateFlows.navigation: Settings → Branch users → Assign a role
alternateFlows.behaviour: They assign only within their own branch and only to roles at or below their own, since they are the person present when somebody joins (BR-2, BR-3).

alternateFlows.condition: The School Admin attempts to grant a permission not released to their branch
alternateFlows.behaviour: It is refused. A School Admin cannot grant what the Super Admin has not released (BR-3).

alternateFlows.condition: A user types the address of a screen they cannot reach
alternateFlows.behaviour: It is refused. Hiding a menu item is not access control (BR-5).

alternateFlows.condition: One person holds different roles at two branches
alternateFlows.behaviour: The role is held on the branch assignment, so each branch's permissions apply where they are working (BR-7).

alternateFlows.condition: A role is to be retired while users hold it
alternateFlows.behaviour: It is refused until they are reassigned, since a user with no role can do nothing (BR-8).

departures.aspect: Enforced on the server, every request
departures.requirement: The permission check runs server-side on every request without exception. No screen, list, report, export or address is served on the basis that its menu item was hidden.
A refusal returns the same message whatever the reason, so it never confirms that a record exists.
A School Admin can never grant a permission the Super Admin has not released to their branch, nor a role above their own, nor anything outside their branch.
The permission check adds no more than 10 milliseconds to a request, since it runs on every one.
Roles, permission changes and refused requests are retained 7 years.

openQuestions.question: Is the role hierarchy that decides at or below their own defined anywhere?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified, and the delegation rule depends on it.

openQuestions.question: Are roles defined once across the group, or separately per branch?
openQuestions.assumption: Once across the group as modelled, with permissions released per branch.

openQuestions.question: Can a user hold more than one role at the same branch?
openQuestions.assumption: Not as modelled. One role per assignment.

openQuestions.question: Should a refused request from a typed address be treated differently from one through the menu, since it may indicate probing?
openQuestions.assumption: Both are recorded and the report distinguishes them, but nothing acts on it.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
